items.behavior: Face tracking is active continuously from app startup, with no model tool call required
items.verification: Dev + robot run: tracking active immediately after launch; log shows no head_tracking tool call
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): NO head_tracking tool call anywhere in a 6-minute DEBUG-level run — the only occurrences of the name are tool registration ('Found 12 tools to load', 'Loaded core tool: head_tracking', 'tool registered'), never 'Tool call received — tool_name=head_tracking'. Daemon-side tracking was nevertheless already RUNNING before anything was asked of it, proven by a CPU A/B on the daemon worker process (pid 4480) after the three evidence turns: as-left-by-the-app 10.4% of a core -> POST /api/media/tracking/disable -> 6.1% -> POST /api/media/tracking/enable -> 8.2%. The as-left state matches the explicitly-enabled state and is ~40% above the disabled state, so the YuNet FaceTracker thread the app started at boot (main.py:374 movement_manager.set_head_tracking(True) -> moves.py:380 start_head_tracking(weight=1.0)) was genuinely active; no 'Head-tracking toggle failed' warning app-side and no 'Cannot enable head tracking: no camera available' warning daemon-side. GET /api/media/tracking/face answered 200 on all 7 polls but always with face_target {detected:false,x:null,y:null,roll:null,ts:null} — and that endpoint is STRUCTURALLY DEAD on mockup-sim: _face_target is only ever written by step_head_tracking(), which is called solely from daemon/backend/robot/backend.py:249; the mockup_sim run loop (mockup_sim/backend.py:73) never calls it, so no face can ever be reported and the head never actually aims on the dev box. What the webcam saw is moot for the same reason, and was in any case the host's IR camera (see DEMO-3). OPERATOR PASS PENDING: the live-face half — that the head visibly follows a real face from startup on the real robot, where step_head_tracking() does run.

items.behavior: After the 1200 ms pre-greeting wake check misses (14/14 boots since 2026-08-24 did), a bounded extended window keeps looking for FACE_WAKE_EXTENDED_MS (default 8000, clamp 0–20000, 0 disables) after the greeting is queued, and on a hit injects a context item so Reachy greets the person by name late. It runs once per app start, honors the FACE_AUTO_GREET kill switch, closes silently the moment the user speaks (a context item landing mid-turn could steer the answer), aborts if the session reconnects, and is cancelled-and-awaited at shutdown — recognition never becomes a continuous scan (D-013).
items.verification: On-robot: boot with nobody in frame, then lean into frame within 8 s without speaking. Journal must show the quick check missing, then `Extended wake face check: recognized <name> (score …) on round N; queued a late named greeting.` and a spoken greeting using the name. Negative control (nobody in frame at all): the window must end with `Extended wake face check: no recognition in N round(s); window closed.` — proving the bound. Speaking immediately after boot must instead produce no injection at all.
